📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’re feeling a bit under the weather, but you don’t want to lose the momentum of your fitness routine. So, should you push through and hit the gym, or is it better to rest and let your body heal? Let’s break it down!

Sleep is the best way to help your body recover swiftly when you’re sick. But if you’re determined to rise and grind, you could use the “neck check” to decide whether to lace up those sneakers or stay in bed.

Many sports doctors use this theory to say that if your symptoms are above the neck — sniffles, sore throat, or a mild headache — you’re generally good to go for a light workout. But if you’re dealing with chest congestion, a hacking or juicy cough, diarrhea, a fever, or an upset stomach, it’s better to take some time to catch up on your Netflix watchlist.

Significant disclaimer: there’s little scientific evidence behind the “neck check,” so use your best judgment.

If you’re going with the above-the-neck rule, exercising with the following symptoms is probably okay.

Going super hard if you have a mild cold is not a good idea. But a light workout, like a walk or a chill Peloton sesh, can be a great way to stay active without overdoing it. Stretching or light yoga might also do the trick.

According to recent reports, stick to light activities like walking for most earaches. Avoid intense workouts like weightlifting, yoga, or pilates, as they can throw off your balance and put pressure on your sinuses, exacerbating the pain.

Light and short workouts are likely fine if your sore throat is mild and lacks fever, cough, or swallowing concerns. Remember to stay hydrated — it can ease your sore throat and is beneficial during exercise.

Light activities like brisk walks or gentle bike rides can help for allergy-related stuffy noses. If your nose is blocked, stick to very light activities, focusing on breathing. Skip workouts if you have a fever, chest congestion, or a productive cough with phlegm until you’re symptom-free.

If you’re experiencing the following symptoms, the workout can wait.

Working out with a fever increases dehydration risk and can worsen the fever. Plus, fever saps your muscle strength and coordination, making you more prone to injuries. So, do yourself a favor and skip the workout until you’re back to normal.

An occasional cough is your body’s way of clearing out irritants, but a frequent or phlegmy cough could signal a respiratory infection like a cold, flu, or even pneumonia or asthma. While a tickle-induced cough isn’t a gym deal-breaker, a persistent one is.

Diarrhea and vomiting can dehydrate you, and physical activity only makes that dehydration worse. Feeling weak? That’s a recipe for injury. Plus, stomach bugs are highly contagious. If you feel antsy, stick to light stretching or yoga at home.

In a recent development, the flu hits your respiratory system hard, with symptoms like fever, chills, sore throat, body aches, fatigue, headache, cough, and congestion. If you’ve got the flu, take it easy and give your body some well-earned R&R.

Once symptom-free, ease back into exercise gradually. Start with less intense workouts to avoid overdoing it. As your symptoms fade, you can gradually return to normal activity.

It has been revealed that regular exercise may shorten recovery time, particularly for acute respiratory infections. Listen to your body’s signals to gauge your strength. If you’re still contagious, opt for home or outdoor workouts, so you don’t spread those germs to fellow gym-goers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As creative software races toward increased automation, are we as designers asking the right questions?

Over the years, I’ve watched the conversations of web developers and designers shift increasingly toward technology, and further away from something we once took great pride in: Craft.

Industry observers note that the 20th century was an extraordinary period for graphic design, particularly typography and print. By the 1990s we had inherited an astonishingly mature digital toolbox: QuarkXPress, Photoshop, PostScript typography and all the precision that came with them.

Those tools were deeply rooted in the crafts they replaced. Photoshop borrowed directly from the photographic darkroom – dodge, burn and all. Quark brought centuries of typographic practice into the digital workspace, giving designers extraordinarily precise control over type and composition.

Then we moved communications to the web – and somehow left much of that toolbox behind. Our web platforms never came close to giving designers the same depth of control. Many creatives simply accepted the loss and stated, “Well, that’s just the web.”.

I never quite bought into that. Instead I started making notes for what would become Design Studio for Gutenberg (DSG), a powerful designer-first plugin for WordPress Gutenberg.

And at this moment, an inflection point when creative software makers increasingly want to automate design itself, we need to ask: Could better tools offer another way forward?

Web typography has always been a particular sore point for me.

I’ll admit my standards may be unusually high. I cut my typography chops as a Type Director at J. Walter Type, part of the legendary JWT ad agency, and such training is hard to shake.

According to recent reports, so I found workarounds for maintaining the quality my clients expected. For example, for notable headlines I would often set the type in Illustrator, kern it properly, export it as SVG artwork and bring that into a website as art.

Ridiculous? Perhaps. But my clients included brands like American Express, Merck and Lincoln Center. They expected high-quality work, and I delivered. But there had to be a better way.

In a recent development, as each latest web-design platform arrived, I would look to see whether somebody had finally built one from a designer’s point of view. A typographer's point of view. Many claimed they had. But mostly they just gave us what programmers thought designers wanted.

Eventually I stopped waiting. A few years ago I sat down with my studio’s programmers and gave them a simple directive:We are going to build what designers need.

WordPress was the obvious foundation. It was open source, mature and unlikely to disappear like so many web-dev programs before it.

My other directive: Design Studio could not be another heavy page-builder sitting on top of WordPress. It needed to live inside Gutenberg and thus benefit from WordPress’ lighter weight and faster core.

In a recent development, we even created our own mantra: WordPress Builds Webpages. DSG Designs Them.

Recent findings suggest that we methodically broke down what was missing. The list grew fast.

We ultimately ended up creating a system with THREE BLOCKS, one custom TEMPLATE, and more UI additions and tools than I could count.

Let’s start with the three blocks, which contain tools you simply will not find in other web-development systems:.

This text block is unique. It has every major type control that you might have found in Quark or InDesign. Powerful tools like KERNING, without which we can never hope to produce professional grade typography.

According to recent reports, font choices in TDB are not tied to any template. Instead they allow full font and style selections just like a desktop app. And it works directly with our font management system found in the DESIGNER DASH backend (more on that later).

It also allows mixed type, font, style and more, all within a single text container.

It has been revealed that A friend testing DSG at a major ad agency mentioned it best: “Composite layers in WP? Mind blown.”.

Sources indicate that import multilayer Photoshop or Krita files (see my comparison of those two here), then treat each layer independently with blur, invert, halftone, sepia and full BLEND settings. Then each layer can be easily scaled, rotated, and even placed anywhere on the page.

This tool is simply fun. Go play with it in our LIVE DEMO.

This full-width block offers real freedom. Starting with a HEIGHT CONTROL slider, so no more needing to wedge in spacers or scaffolding.

Within the Composition Block, TDB and ADB can be placed freely anywhere you want. Even overlapping each other, or hanging off the CB. (Our website is the perfect example.).

Some early testers had to look twice to make sure they were still in WordPress.

Industry observers note that we knew just what they meant: Rulers, Guides, Grid, device-specific Visibility icons across every object in the List View. We include a very special BLANK CANVAS template, better page controls, and a backend DESIGNER DASH with tabs for Font.

My goal here isn’t to catalog every Design Studio for Gutenberg feature. I mention these to make a larger point: Web designers deserve better tools. And that feels particularly important now.

AI has an enormous role to play in our future creative work. Let it remove drudgery, generate first passes, organise assets and automate anything that doesn’t benefit from human judgment.

Sources indicate that but craft begins where the default answer ends. “Craft” has always been, and shall always remain a very human thing.

It has been revealed that craft is deciding that two letters need to be kerned tighter. That an image needs to move three pixels down. That this composition should deliberately break the grid. That the mobile version shouldn’t simply be a smaller copy of the desktop.

Industry observers note that those are precisely the kinds of decisions that only professional designers should make. And it requires precision tools like those in DSG that allow such decisions to be executed.

After reading the DSG manual, I asked ChatGPT how its own web-building abilities compared with those of a competent designer using DSG. Its answer was spot-on:.

“A surprising amount of what DSG enables is still awkward to get from AI.” — ChatGPT.

It has been revealed that in my mind it is not a question of human vs. AI. But instead, how to use the best tools for each part of your job.

According to recent reports, we built a live demo so you can come kick the tires. And because we are very significant on sharing in general, and the open source, free and affordable software movements, we are releasing Design Studio for Gutenberg, with everything we have talked about and so much more for just $39. Including per-person unlimited use (right, that means no more counting websites), and a license that never expires.

It has been revealed that with the release of Design Studio 1.0 we hope to contribute to the goal of building a better web. This is step one.

Visit Design Studio for Gutenberg, try the DEMO: https://openstudiony.com.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a popular supplement promising muscle gains and enhanced performance.
  • Creatine monohydrate is a naturally occurring substance found in muscle cells.
  • Although you can find creatine in foods like red meat and seafood, many gym enthusiasts and athletes boost their stores with supplements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ah, creatine! It’s a popular supplement promising muscle gains and enhanced performance. But as you’re hitting the gym harder and seeing results, there are some potential side effects to be aware of. Here’s the lowdown.

Creatine monohydrate is a naturally occurring substance found in muscle cells. It helps to produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP) — your muscles’ go-to fuel when working hard.

Although you can find creatine in foods like red meat and seafood, many gym enthusiasts and athletes boost their stores with supplements. Why? Because more creatine equals more ATP, which means more energy for high-intensity activities. More fuel means more mileage!

Sources indicate that now, here’s where things get hairy. You might dial up your body’s DHT (dihydrotestosterone) production when you uplevel creatine. DHT is a derivative of testosterone and plays a big-league role in developing male characteristics. But here’s the catch: while DHT might beef up your alpha vibe, it’s also notorious for thinning out hairlines in peeps predisposed to male pattern baldness.

In a recent development, so, do creatine supplements cause baldness? Maybe! The buzz mainly stems from a small 2009 study where college-aged rugby players loaded up on creatine and saw their DHT levels increase significantly.

In a recent development, because DHT can shrink hair follicles and shorten the hair growth cycle, it may seem logical to blame creatine for contributing to hair thinning. However, it’s crucial to remember that these findings are a one-hit wonder — they haven’t been seen again in other studies. Plus, let’s not forget that intense workouts alone can pump up these hormones, too.

As a result, the jury’s still out, making the creatine-and-baldness saga a hot topic for gym gossip and scientists alike.

The same 2009 study found that after a week of taking high-dose creatinine at 25 grams per day, DHT levels rose by 56%. When the researchers dropped the dose to 5g daily for two more weeks, levels remained 40% higher than baseline. These findings contrasted with the control group participants who took a placebo.

It has been revealed that does this mean creatine could spell disaster for your do? Well, creatine boosts DHT, the usual suspect in male pattern baldness, also called androgenic alopecia. However, your disposition to hair loss and the effects of DHT is genetic, meaning that it’s inherited.

Sources indicate that some folks are more prone to DHT’s hair-ruffling effects because of how their androgen receptor gene is wired. Hormones like testosterone and DHT bind to androgen receptors, typically triggering normal hair growth. However, variations in the AR gene make the androgens extra effective, making you more likely to experience hair loss.

So, while there isn’t much evidence to say that creatine supplements cause hair loss, the connection to increased DHT levels is worth considering if your family reunions look like a convention for bald eagles.

In a recent development, beyond the potential for a breezy scalp, creatine is actually solid in the safety department, with long-term studies giving it a thumbs up. However, although creatinine doesn’t pose a risk to healthy individuals, it might not be your best move if you have kidney, high blood pressure, or liver disease.

Another thing to keep in mind is that creatinine loves to hang onto water, so expect some extra bloat and weigh-in surprises as your body adjusts.

Thinking of starting a creatine kick? Chatting with your doctor first is always wise, especially if you have other health conditions or take medications. They can advise you and rule out any potential interactions.

It has been revealed that if you’re taking creatinine and notice changes to your hair, a check-up is a good idea. Shedding a few strands is normal, but it’s a red flag if you start losing clumps of hair. Rapid hair loss can indicate underlying health problems that go beyond your hairstyle.

According to recent reports, furthermore, consult a doctor if hair loss is weighing on your mind. They can offer solutions or treatments to manage your hair loss and stress.

According to recent reports, creatine is celebrated for its muscle-building prowess, but rumors of a link with hair loss exist. The good news is there’s little conclusive evidence directly connecting creatine supplementation to permanent hair loss.

However, creatine loading may boost DHT levels, a hormone linked to male pattern baldness, especially in people genetically predisposed to hair thinning.

So, if you’re concerned about hair loss, it might be wise to talk with a doctor before adding creatine supplements to your muscle-building routine.

10 Signs You Might Not Really Be in Love: How to Tell the Difference

📅 26 Jun 2024 | ⏱️ 3 min read (692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing.
  • Wondering how to tell the difference?
  • Feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing. Are you truly in love or just caught in a wave of infatuation? Sometimes, what seems like a heart-thumping romance may be a fleeting crush.

Wondering how to tell the difference? We’ve got you! Here’s a rundown of the 10 signs you’re not really in love.

Feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo? That’s pretty normal. But before you start planning your future or picking out matching Halloween costumes, you may wanna make sure it’s real love and not a case of a serious crush.

Here are some signs that you may not really be in love:.

Caught up in the romance novel vibe? If you’re all about the feelings of being in love rather than who’s sharing your popcorn, it might just be that you’re smitten with the idea of love itself.

Time to check if your relationship is more about the fairy tale than the real person.

Chatting with your partner shouldn’t feel as shallow as a kiddie pool. If deep talks are tougher than pulling teeth and rarer than a unicorn, it’s a red flag.

Sticking to small talk about the weather and dinner aims suggests the emotional depth for a lasting bond might be missing.

When discussions about future intends feel as far-fetched as sci-fi adventures, they may reveal underlying doubts about the relationship’s viability.

Industry observers note that if imagining a future together feels unrealistic or undesirable, it’s time to ask yourself why. Real love looks a future; infatuation lives for the weekend.

Remember when their sock on the floor was cute? If little quirks now make you more cranky than charmed, it might mean the love goggles are off, your feelings have shifted from affection to annoyance, and the reality check has bounced.

Love is seeing imperfections and adoring them anyway.

Recent findings suggest that feeling more at ease or more ‘yourself’ when your partner isn’t around is a telling sign. If you’re secretly throwing mini-parties when they leave the room, you need to stop and think. Real-deal love means missing their chaos when they’re gone, not celebrating the silence.

Sources indicate that shared values are the anchor of deep, lasting relationships. If your core values clash more than a polka dot and stripes ensemble, you’re in for a rough ride, as finding common ground could be challenging!

Lasting love grows from shared beliefs and mutual respect, not from opposing battle lines.

No respect? No future. Respect is as critical to love as air is to breathing. Without mutual respect, you might just be coexisting rather than genuinely connecting.

If you no longer admire or respect each other’s opinions and choices, sustaining a healthy relationship will be difficult.

Recent findings suggest that if they’re out of sight and totally out of mind, that’s not just independence — it might be indifference. When love is real, you should long for their laugh or lame jokes when they’re away. Could it be that your emotional attachment isn’t as strong as it should be for a lasting relationship?

According to recent reports, if your best moments are consistently away from your partner, your heart might not be in it to win it. Perhaps your relationship isn’t providing enough support or happiness.

True love enriches your life and doesn’t play second fiddle to your social circle. It’s time to evaluate where your emotional energy is invested.

Still window shopping while you’re supposedly locked down? It’s a sign you might not be all in. A love that lasts doesn’t keep a backup catalog — it’s too busy loving what it already has.

Knowing why you’re still scanning for alternatives can help you address what might be missing or unfulfilled in your relationship.

Are you genuinely in love or just in love with being in love? If you’re secretly thrilled when they’re not around, stuck in surface-level chit-chat, or dreading deep-future talks, these are cosmic signs that it’s rethink o’clock.

Don’t ignore the signals — tuning in now can save you heartache later and lead you toward a love that genuinely fulfills you.

Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home. Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up! Why are my ears clogged? Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked: Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage. If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection. Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side. Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too. Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure. Best clogged ear remedies 1. Pop and unclog The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes. 2. Swallow, yawn, or chew The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow. 3. Ear drops Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes. Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful. 4. Warmth and gravity To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily. 5. Hit the steam room Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 6. Take allergy medication Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears. Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort. 7. Rinse away the gunk Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing. When to see your doctor Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention. What not to do when you have clogged ears Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries. Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion. Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation. Takeaway Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies. Tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:.

Sources indicate that tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

These tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:.

Sources indicate that tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Recent findings suggest that want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

It has been revealed that tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

It has been revealed that these zesty little superheroes are your gut’s newly introduced best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

Tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

Recent findings suggest that flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

It has been revealed that but wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Recent findings suggest that keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related issues and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

From giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as rumours about the casting of the next James Bond began to hot up this week, my phone has been busy. Most of my friends (hello, both!) know me as a huge James Bond fan, and have wanted to know who I thought was going to get the role. Well, one thing's for sure, I told them all. It won't be Pattinson. Mark my words. He's just too famous.

Recent findings suggest that so you can imagine my surprise when Robert Pattinson was indeed announced as the upcoming James Bond this afternoon. Everything about the news feels bizarre to me, including the lack of press release and associated fanfare (whereas Daniel Craig rode down the Thames on a speedboat, Pattinson was announced via a simple social media post). But the biggest shock is that Pattinson is by far the most famous person to be cast in the role. He's the first bonafide A-lister to pick up the Walther PPK. He's Batman, for God's sake. For better or worse, the Bond brand changed forever today. And it's thanks to one name: Amazon.

It has been revealed that it perhaps isn't surprising that Blofeld's—sorry, Bezos's—company has opted for such a bankable star. The company paid billions to acquire MGM (which owned the rights to Bond), and will want a return on its investment. But the whole thing seems so at odds with the ethos of the previous Bond custodians. "I felt I had to have an unknown actor, not a star," producer Cubby Broccoli remarked of the search for the very first Bond. "Above all, a man you’d believe could be James Bond.".

In a recent development, for decades, Bond has been one of the most carefully controlled brands in entertainment. The gun barrel sequence, the theme tune, the 007 logo, the Aston Martin; every element is instantly recognisable, and has been meticulously protected by the Broccoli family. Bond films have always felt like events, partly because they don't come along very often. But Amazon doesn't do scarcity, it does content. And with the company now in creative control of the franchise, it's hard not to wonder how long it will be before 007 becomes less of a cinematic institution and more of an endlessly expandable IP. I'm not sure I'm ready for the 'Young Q' spin-off.

It has been revealed that there are, of course, opportunities here. Bond has arguably been in need of a shake-up for some time, and Pattinson is a genuinely exciting actor, capable of bringing something strange, unpredictable and perhaps even uncomfortable to a character that has occasionally felt trapped by his own iconography. But the choice also feels like a statement of intent from Amazon. Where previous Bond actors were largely blank canvases onto which the 007 identity could be projected, Pattinson arrives with a huge, established brand of his own. Rather than making a star out of Bond, Amazon has bought a star to sell Bond. It's a subtle distinction, but a significant one. Am I going to be able to look up at the screen and see James Bond, rather than Robert Pattinson in a suit?

According to recent reports, but while it'll be Pattinson's name that hogs the headlines, the bigger question isn't simply what kind of Bond Pattinson will be, but what kind of brand Amazon wants Bond to become. Will the manufacturer recognise that Bond's enduring appeal lies partly in his exclusivity, his mystique, and his ability to remain just a little out of reach? For all of his reinventions, 007 has always felt bigger than the actor playing him. Until today.

Relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns. From the first flush of love to the settled comfort of commitment, relationships have stages that evolve with time.

Industry observers note that each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build. Understanding the dynamics of these stages is crucial for any couple (or throuple!) aiming to develop a lasting bond.

Whether you’re in the throes of a latest romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.

Recent findings suggest that from those “can’t eat, can’t sleep” early days to the “let’s build an empire” moments, each relationship stage is like a season of your fave drama binge. But, like any good drama, the plot thickens as time passes and things change. Here’s what to expect, month by month:.

Welcome to the love bubble, where everything about your significant other seems nothing short of magical. The positives overshadow any negatives, creating a blissfully skewed balance sheet of love. It lasts from about 6 months to 2 years for most peeps, but many folks say they are still madly in love even after 20 years together!

Sources indicate that research reveals that during this stage, the prefrontal cortex, which is crucial for critically judging others, shows decreased activity. In other words, you’re less likely to focus on your partner’s faults and more likely to overlook their flaws.

According to recent reports, lurve also activates specific areas in the brain that are driven by goals and rewards. These areas are rich in dopamine and oxytocin receptors, chemicals that make you feel good and bonded to others. They encourage you to pursue and maintain a relationship because it feels rewarding and fulfilling.

In a recent development, if the euphoric stage is the wild, pulse-racing party of love, the early attachment stage is the cozy after-party where things get real comfortable. In the thrilling initial phase, your brain is doped up on dopamine, but as this initial buzz begins to mellow, a more sophisticated part of the brain starts to step up — the ventral pallidum.

Now, after the first year or so, deeper bonds are formed, helped along by attachment hormones like vasopressin and oxytocin, also fondly known as “the love hormone.” These hormones help transform the electric excitement of newly introduced love into a warm, enduring attachment.

Industry observers note that hold tight because the crisis stage hits around 5 to 7 years, and it’s a true test of your relationship’s resilience. This phase often feels like a rollercoaster, where life’s challenges can either pull you apart or push you closer together. Many couples experience a drift during this time, and how you handle it — either by addressing the challenges head-on or continuing to drift — can define your future together.

Recent findings suggest that significant life events, like becoming parents, often occur during this stage and can intensify the pressure. These events can either strengthen your bond through shared responsibilities and mutual love or strain it to the breaking point. Successfully navigating this stage means moving beyond mere survival to fostering a deeper, more meaningful connection.

According to recent reports, if you’ve made it this far, congrats, you’re in the deep attachment stage! Post-crisis, you’re looking at 7 years and beyond where you settle into that deep, comfy love. No more daily fireworks — now it’s about a slow-burning ember that warms the house.

You know each other inside and out, warts and all. It’s about unconditional support, knowing looks across crowded rooms, and being each other’s rock. Welcome to the good life!

According to recent reports, every relationship is a blend of sweet and sour and everything in between. Understanding the stages, from the initial euphoria to the deep attachment stage, helps you embrace the journey, keep your bond strong, and prepare your heart for whatever comes next. So buckle up and enjoy the ride — it’ll be worth it!

It has been revealed that protein farts are a common, albeit smelly, side effect of high-protein diets. They happen because of how proteins are digested. But(t) don’t worry! We have some tips to help you say goodbye to those pungent protein toots without giving up your gains.

Industry observers note that protein farts are episodes of flatulence that don’t smell too pleasant! They’re generally due to upping your protein intake from supplements like protein shakes.

And while these butt whistles may be embarrassing, you’ll be glad to know they’re generally harmless.

Farts consist of different gases. The most stinky odors usually come from your gut bacteria, producing sulfur-containing compounds as they break down food. The main culprit is hydrogen sulfide, which gives off a characteristic rotten egg smell, yum!

But why do your protein choices lead to thunder from down under?

According to recent reports, well, there’s not much evidence that a high-protein diet causes protein farts. However, there’s some anecdotal evidence that supplementary protein — like protein bars, protein shakes, and powder powders — increases flatulence, but it’s likely due to non-protein ingredients like lactose.

Supplements containing whey protein or casein are derived from milk and are high in lactose, which can increase flatulence. If your body can’t properly digest lactose, it ends up in your colon, where bacteria feast on it, producing — you guessed it — more gas and cheek flapping.

So, whey protein can throw a curveball for those who are lactose intolerant or sensitive. Surprisingly, it might also stir up digestive drama even for folks who typically handle dairy like champs, potentially due to additives like fart-inducing sweeteners or thickeners.

In a recent development, some people may also have more significant complications digesting protein. Proteins are significant, complex molecules — breaking them down is no small task for your gut. Plant-based protein supplements, like those based on soya beans, may also worsen flatulence.

FYI: Another reason why flatulence is common with protein powders and supplements is due to the addition of artificial sweeteners in the powders and bars, like sugar alcohols, sucralose, sorbitol, xylitol, and stevia.

If you’re looking to continue your protein regimen without becoming a walking, talking whoopee cushion, here are some strategic adjustments you can make:.

Don’t just dive into the deep end with your protein intake — wade in slowly. Gradually increasing the amount of protein you consume allows your digestive system to adjust without getting overwhelmed. This step-by-step approach can help minimize the likelihood of excessive gas.

Industry observers note that keep the water flowing. Drinking plenty of water is crucial as it helps your digestive system handle higher protein levels more efficiently. Proper hydration aids in the breakdown and absorption of nutrients, which can help prevent gas buildup.

Sometimes, your body needs a little extra help. Enzyme supplements like Beano or Lactaid can be game-changers, especially if you consume proteins that your body struggles with. These supplements help break down proteins and lactose, making digestion smoother and less gassy.

Industry observers note that variety isn’t just the spice of life — it can also be the solution to your protein fart problems. If whey protein tends to upset your stomach, explore other options like plant-based or animal-based proteins that might be easier to digest. Diversifying your protein sources can also ensure you get a broad range of nutrients.

It has been revealed that what you blend your protein powder with can make a big difference. If you’re whipping up a protein shake, be mindful of adding high-fiber fruits and vegetables, as these can also increase gas production. Try to find a balance that allows you to enjoy the benefits of protein and fiber without the extra flatulence.

Introducing probiotics into your diet can improve your gut health, which can help manage and reduce gas production. Whether through supplements or probiotic-rich foods like yogurt, kefir, or sauerkraut, boosting your gut flora can aid in better overall digestion and less discomfort from gas.

It has been revealed that protein farts are a rather windy side effect of a high-protein diet, but they don’t have to knock you off course. Try easing into your protein consumption, staying hydrated, diversifying your protein sources, and integrating enzyme supplements or probiotics to max those gains, minus the stink bombs!

Originally popular in men’s hairstyling, the undercut has crossed gender boundaries and gained popularity among peeps seeking a hairstyle that stands out.

It’s a style that offers a stark contrast and is often used to add an edge to an otherwise conventional look. So whether it’s a side undercut, undercut pixie, mullet undercut, or nape undercut, these hairstyles for women, men, and folks of all genders enhance individuality while offering practical benefits like reduced drying time and less hair maintenance.

Choosing an undercut means embracing a hairstyle with a “heady” mix of aesthetic and practical benefits. Here’s why an undercut might be the refreshing change you need.

This trimmed-down approach is a time-saver and reduces the daily wear and tear from blow dryers and straighteners, keeping hair healthier in the long run.

Undercuts reduce your scalp’s weight and improve hair follicle airflow. This keeps the scalp cooler and reduces the buildup of sweat and oil that can lead to scalp irritation, dermatitis, and dandruff. As a result, undercuts could lead to more robust, healthier hair growth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hickeys, or as scientists call them, subdermal hematomas, are love’s graffiti. If you’ve ever scrambled for scarves or turtlenecks, welcome to the kissing booth of knowledge! Join us as we navigate the lifecycle of hickeys, from their eye-catching start to their subtle fade, and learn how to speed up their departure.

A hickey, medically known as a subdermal contusion or hematoma, is simply a bruise that forms as a result of vigorous kissing or sucking on soft skin, typically around the neck. This intense suction causes the tiny blood vessels under the skin, a.k.a. capillaries, to burst and release blood into the surrounding tissues. The immediate result? An unmistakable red or purple mark that gradually shifts to a darker shade as it heals.

From a medical standpoint, hickeys are intriguing. They showcase the skin’s sensitivity and the body’s rapid response to minor vascular injury. Not so romantic when you think about it scientifically, right? But hey, it’s all part of the human experience of showing affection — or something like that.

When you get a hickey, your body starts a healing process that resembles how it deals with other bruises. Here’s a more detailed look at each stage of a hickey’s life cycle.

Immediately after the passionate moment, a hickey appears on the skin, screaming in shades of bright red or deep purple. This initial coloration is due to blood from the ruptured capillaries pooling beneath the skin’s surface in response to the suction. It’s your skin’s way of signaling that there’s been some minor internal damage in that area.

As the hickey begins to heal, it undergoes a whole wardrobe of color transformations, showcasing your body’s metabolic process at work.

Initially, the hickey darkens as the blood begins to oxidize. Then, after a few days, the body starts to break down and reabsorb the blood, so it turns lighter — going from blue to green to brown and, finally, mellow yellow. This rainbow journey reflects the breakdown of hemoglobin, the iron-containing substance in the blood, into biliverdin and bilirubin.

According to recent reports, finally, your hickey starts to ghost you. Over a week or two, depending on factors like your skin type, overall health, how severe the hickey was., and how your body rides the healing waves, the last traces of your hickey fade into nothing.

During this stage, the body’s immune system clears away the remaining by-products of the broken-down blood. White blood cells swoop in like a cleanup crew at a festival, gobbling up and digesting the debris in a process called phagocytosis, while increased blood flow to the area helps to flush out the remnants.

According to recent reports, need a hickey gone yesterday? Here’s how to help your hickey heal. Start with a cold pack — grab a spoon from the freezer or a chilled gel pack and gently press it against your hickey. This will help reduce any swelling and scatter the blood pooling under your skin, which can help minimize that bold bruise.

After using cold treatment for the first 48 hours, it’s time to turn up the heat. Switch to warm compresses to get the blood flowing smoothly again. A few minutes a few times a day invites more circulation to the hickey zone, helping you hustle through healing and clear out the blood remnants more swiftly.

You can also try a dab of comfrey ointment. Research highlights it may reduce bruise size and coloration for some peeps.

It has been revealed that caught off guard? A little concealer or foundation over the hickey makes it less noticeable.

In a recent development, not into makeup? Scarves and high-necked shirts are also great accessories for your camouflage arsenal.

Typically, a hickey will last anywhere from 5 days to 2 weeks, depending on its severity and your body’s healing capabilities.

In a recent development, communication is key! Let your partner know your feelings about receiving a hickey — some might find it fun, while others may prefer to keep their necks clear.

In a recent development, while generally harmless, hickeys can sometimes lead to complications like skin infections or, very rarely, blood clots. It’s best to keep the affection gentle to avoid any concerns.

Hickeys are nothing more than bruises in disguise. They start as bright red to purple love stamps and gradually fade over several days to a couple of weeks. Speed up the process with heat and cold packs or a splodge of comfrey cream.

It has been revealed that remember, the best approach to handling hickeys — like all aspects of relationships — is communication and care. So go forth, love responsibly, and keep a scarf handy, just in case!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

In a recent development, picture this: you've just landed in Honolulu after a long transcontinental flight. You've got four days on Maui planned, and then a few nights on Kauai before heading home. The problem? Those interisland flights add up fast — Hawaiian Airlines will gladly charge you $150–$250 *per person* for a 20-to-40-minute hop between islands. For a family of four, that's easily $600–$1,000 in airfare just to island-hop, on top of everything else you've already spent to get to Hawaii. Now imagine paying 7,500 HawaiianMiles per person instead — miles you transferred from your American Express Membership Rewards account at a 1:1 ratio just a day or two before booking. Suddenly, that $150–$250 ticket costs you points worth less than a nice dinner. At 3.3 cents per point on the high end, you're extracting extraordinary value from miles that most people leave sitting in an account doing nothing. This is what the ChooseFI community means when we talk about finding pricing inefficiencies in loyalty programs. Hawaiian Airlines prices these interisland segments on a dynamic award chart — but because these are short, regional hops operated almost entirely on 717s and A321s between islands most people aren't cross-shopping for redemptions, the program hasn't inflated the price the way major international carriers have. The sweet spot holds. The math is simple and satisfying: a cash ticket from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) or Lihue, Kauai (LIH) typically runs $100–$250. You're redeeming 7,500 miles to cover that cost, which means you're getting **1.3 to 3.3 cents per point** in value — above what most programs deliver on domestic redemptions. And because Hawaiian charges **zero fuel surcharges** on its own-operated flights, every mile goes toward the ticket price, not toward fees. For the FI-minded traveler who planned a multi-island Hawaii trip anyway, this redemption doesn't just save money — it reframes how you think about points. These aren't bonuses. They're a currency, and knowing where to spend them is the skill.

The core insight here is deceptively simple: HawaiianMiles prices interisland flights at a flat 7,500 miles in economy, and that price is shockingly stable relative to what these tickets actually cost in cash.

It has been revealed that here's why this works as a pricing inefficiency. Hawaiian Airlines operates a near-monopoly on interisland travel in Hawaii. There's limited true competition for these routes (go! Mokulele operates turboprops on some routes, but Hawaiian dominates the jet service). Because cash demand is inelastic — visitors need to get between islands — Hawaiian charges a premium in cash. But the HawaiianMiles award program hasn't kept pace with those cash price increases in the same aggressive way that programs like United MileagePlus or Delta SkyMiles have. The result: 7,500 miles per segment, consistently, while cash prices climb.

Now let's talk about how you actually get those miles into your account.

The primary transfer path the ChooseFI community uses is American Express Membership Rewards → HawaiianMiles at a 1:1 ratio. If you have the Amex Gold, Platinum, or a no-annual-fee Amex Everyday card earning MR points, you can transfer directly to Hawaiian. Transfer speed is 1–2 days — not instant, so proposal accordingly and don't wait until the last minute.

Two other paths exist if you're working with different currencies:.

One critical nuance: HawaiianMiles are earned primarily through flying, not credit card spend. Hawaiian does have a co-branded credit card, but it's not a top earner for most people's daily spend. This means your primary accumulation strategy is transfer partners — Amex MR and Bilt are your best levers.

Another key detail: Hawaiian miles never expire. This matters because you can slowly accumulate miles across multiple statement cycles, transfer when you're ready to book, and not feel rushed. There's no expiration clock running against you.

Finally, the no fuel surcharges policy is a genuine differentiator. Many programs — particularly those involving European carriers — tack on $300–$600 in surcharges that gut your redemption's net value. HawaiianMiles charges no fuel surcharges on Hawaiian-operated flights. Your 7,500 miles covers the flight. Taxes and fees on interisland tickets are minimal, often just a few dollars. What you see is what you get.

It has been revealed that go to hawaiianairlines.com and use the 'Book' tool, selecting 'Reward Travel' as your travel type. Enter your route — for example, HNL to OGG (Honolulu to Kahului, Maui) or HNL to LIH (Honolulu to Lihue, Kauai). Plug in your desired travel date and search. You're looking for economy award space priced at 7,500 miles. Availability on interisland routes is almost always wide open — this is one of the best availability scores (5/5) of any sweet spot in this guide series, but it costs nothing to confirm before you transfer.

If you don't have a HawaiianMiles account, create one at hawaiianairlines.com — it takes about two minutes and is free. Note your HawaiianMiles number. You'll need it for the transfer step.

From Marriott Bonvoy: Use this only as a last resort due to the 3:1 ratio. Navigate to Bonvoy's transfer portal and select HawaiianMiles. Allow up to 5 days.

HawaiianMiles opens its booking window 330 days out. If you're planning a Hawaii trip far in advance and have specific flight times in mind, you can search and book early. That remarked, given the excellent availability on these routes, booking 2–4 weeks out is usually fine.

Sources indicate that this is rare for interisland routes, but if it happens, try: searching adjacent dates, looking at different departure times on the same route, or checking alternate routing (e.g., OGG to LIH instead of HNL to LIH directly). Interisland availability doesn't fluctuate the way transatlantic business class does.

According to recent reports, card links may earn ChooseFI a commission. See our advertiser disclosure.

Let's make this concrete. You're planning a two-week Hawaii trip for two people. You've booked your Honolulu arrival flight separately, and now you need to connect the dots between islands: Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) mid-trip, and then Maui (OGG) to Lihue, Kauai (LIH) before heading home.

The cash price check: Pull up hawaiianairlines.com and look at what these tickets retail for. On a typical mid-trip travel day, the HNL→OGG segment is priced at $189 per person. The OGG→LIH hop runs $149 per person. For two travelers, that's $676 in cash — before you've bought a single plate of shave ice.

In a recent development, the points price: Each segment costs 7,500 HawaiianMiles per person in economy. Two passengers, two flights: 30,000 HawaiianMiles total, plus roughly $10–$20 in taxes and fees across both bookings. No fuel surcharges.

Industry observers note that the CPP calculation: You're replacing $676 in cash spending with 30,000 miles. That's 2.25 cents per point — well above the 0.8–1.2 cpp you'd expect on typical HawaiianMiles redemptions, and solidly within the 1.3–3.3 cpp sweet spot range for this redemption.

According to recent reports, what the experience looks like: Hawaiian's interisland product is no-frills — these are 20-to-40-minute flights on Boeing 717s. You won't get a meal or premium service. But you will get a reliable, on-time carrier, clean aircraft, and the undeniable satisfaction of hopping between two of the most beautiful island destinations on Earth without opening your wallet at the gate.

For the ChooseFI traveler, the win isn't the in-flight experience — it's the mental accounting shift. You budgeted for interisland flights; now that budget goes to a sunset sailing charter or a snorkeling excursion instead. The points paid for the planes. The cash funds the memories.

Industry observers note that do: Transfer Points in the Right Batch Size HawaiianMiles doesn't allow you to transfer partial miles back out, so calculate exactly how many you need before initiating a transfer. For two passengers on two flights, that's 30,000 miles. Transfer exactly that amount — or a small buffer — rather than dumping your entire MR balance into a program you may not use frequently.

Do: Use Amex MR or Bilt as Your Primary Earning Strategy Since HawaiianMiles are earned primarily through flying, your accumulation blueprint should center on transferable currencies. The Amex Gold Card (4x on dining and groceries) and Amex Platinum (5x on flights) are elite MR earners. Bilt's no-annual-fee card earning on rent is underused by the ChooseFI community for exactly this kind of transfer.

According to recent reports, do: Search for Availability Before You Transfer This is worth repeating as a pro tip because fresh points travelers make this mistake constantly. Transfer speeds are 1–2 days for Amex MR and Bilt. Don't transfer points and then discover the flight you wanted is sold out. Always confirm availability first, then transfer, then book immediately once miles land.

Sources indicate that avoid: Using Marriott Bonvoy for This Transfer At a 3:1 ratio, you'd spend 22,500 Bonvoy points for a 7,500-mile award. Bonvoy points are worth approximately 0.7–0.9 cpp on their own best redemptions. The math doesn't hold here — save your Bonvoy points for hotel redemptions.

Do: Consider the Merger Context Hawaiian Airlines is in the process of merging with Alaska Airlines, and HawaiianMiles may eventually transition into Alaska Mileage Initiative. Pay attention to program announcements. This could change transfer partners, award pricing, or program structure. The current sweet spot exists now — book it while the program operates under its current rules.

In a recent development, avoid: Waiting for a 'Better' Redemption on These Miles HawaiianMiles are a limited-use currency. They're excellent for interisland and mainland-to-Hawaii flights, but they don't transfer to other airlines and don't unlock international business class sweet spots. If you've got miles in this program, use them for exactly what they're designed for — Hawaiian flights — rather than letting them sit hoping for a better opportunity that may never come.

Sources indicate that do: Book Multiple Segments in a Single Trip If you're doing a true multi-island itinerary, every interisland hop is 7,500 miles. Three islands means two hops — 15,000 miles per person. Plan your island sequence to minimize backtracking, and book all segments at once once your miles transfer.

Make multi-island trips affordable with the right points strategy.

Major Hawaiian Islands Connected.

Most visitors to Hawaii stick to one island because interisland flights add $100-$400+ per person to the trip cost. By using points for these short hops, you unlock a fundamentally different Hawaii experience — island-hopping from Oahu to Maui to the Big Island to Kauai without the airfare costs stacking up. This is a multiplier strategy: you are not just saving on one flight, you are enabling an entirely different type of trip. Combining a points-funded mainland-to-Hawaii flight with points-funded interisland hops creates a nearly free (in cash) multi-island Hawaiian vacation.

According to recent reports, decide which islands you want to visit and in what order. The most common combinations are Oahu + Maui, Oahu + Big Island, or a three-island itinerary. Map out how many interisland hops you need so you know the total points required.

Check Hawaiian Airlines (7,500 miles each way), Southwest (variable, typically 4,000-8,000 points), and United (5,000-7,500 miles) for each interisland segment. Southwest often offers the best flexibility with no change fees and no blackout dates.

In a recent development, for Hawaiian Airlines, transfer Amex Membership Rewards. For Southwest, earn Rapid Rewards directly or transfer from Chase (transfer to Southwest is currently limited). For United segments, transfer from Chase or use Turkish Miles&Smiles for even lower pricing.

In a recent development, book each interisland hop as a separate one-way award. This gives you maximum flexibility to mix airlines and optimize pricing per segment. One-way awards have no penalty compared to round trips on these short routes.

According to recent reports, align your interisland hops with your arrival and departure flights. Arrive on one island and depart from a different one (open-jaw booking) to avoid backtracking. For example, arrive Honolulu, hop to Maui, depart Maui to the mainland.

Industry observers note that hawaiian Airlines has the most extensive interisland network and offers the most daily frequencies. Southwest Airlines also operates key interisland routes (Honolulu-Maui, Honolulu-Kona, Honolulu-Lihue). United flies select interisland segments as well. Each airline has different award pricing and transfer partner access.

Sources indicate that hawaiian Airlines interisland awards typically price at 7,500 HawaiianMiles each way. Southwest varies by cash fare but generally costs 4,000-8,000 Rapid Rewards points each way for interisland hops. United interisland segments can be booked for 5,000-7,500 miles using various Star Alliance partner programs.

Industry observers note that yes, especially when booking multiple hops. A family of four making two interisland hops at $150 each way would spend $1,200 in cash. Converting that to points frees up significant cash for accommodations, activities, and dining. The per-point value (1.5-2.5 cents) is reasonable, and the trip flexibility gained is substantial.

A popular strategy is to fly into Honolulu (Oahu), hop to Maui for beaches and Haleakala, then continue to the Big Island (Kona) for volcanoes and snorkeling, and optionally finish on Kauai for dramatic scenery. Each hop is 30-60 minutes. Allow 2-3 days minimum per island.

In a recent development, this redemption was built for families and couples planning a multi-island Hawaii vacation — full stop. If you're visiting multiple islands (which most Hawaii first-timers and repeat visitors do), you're already mentally budgeting for interisland flights. This sweet spot simply redirects that cash budget back into your pocket and replaces it with points.

Families get a 5/5 Family Friendly score here for good reason: availability is wide open, booking is simple, and the economics scale beautifully. Four people, two hops = 60,000 miles to cover potentially $1,200+ in interisland airfare. That's an extraordinary displacement of vacation cash.

Industry observers note that beginners are explicitly welcomed by this redemption's design. There's no partner airline complexity, no fuel surcharge math to calculate, no routing rules to decode. You search on Hawaiian's website, you transfer points, you book. The 5/5 Beginner Friendly and Easy to Book scores reflect that this is genuinely one of the simplest award redemptions you can execute.

Minimum points needed: 7,500 HawaiianMiles per person per segment. For a solo traveler doing two hops, that's 15,000 miles. For a family of four doing two hops, that's 60,000 miles.

According to recent reports, this is NOT for: Travelers who don't have an Amex MR or Bilt account and no path to earning HawaiianMiles swiftly. It's also not ideal for travelers who only need a single interisland flight — the opportunity cost of setting up the transfer relationship for 7,500 miles may not be worth it unless you're already accumulating MR points for other redemptions.

Sources indicate that this redemption earns a **Beginner** rating — and it genuinely deserves it. In a world of waitlists, fuel surcharges, routing rules, and phone-only bookings, Hawaiian interisland awards are refreshingly clean. **What makes it easy:** Award availability is consistently excellent (5/5). The booking portal is functional and user-friendly. There are no fuel surcharges to calculate. Miles never expire, so there's no pressure. You can complete the entire redemption — from transfer initiation to confirmed booking — in about 48 hours. **The one genuine friction point:** Earning HawaiianMiles isn't as straightforward as earning Chase Ultimate Rewards or Amex MR. Hawaiian doesn't have a widely-used co-branded credit card for most people's everyday spend. This means you're dependent on transfer partners, and the Amex MR and Bilt paths are your primary options. If you don't have either, this redemption becomes harder to access. **Tip 1:** Start with an Amex card that earns Membership Rewards — the Amex Gold is the ChooseFI community favorite for everyday earning. Once you're accumulating MR points, you have a direct path to Hawaiian via a 1:1 transfer. **Tip 2:** Always search award availability before transferring. It takes 30 seconds and protects you from the one mistake that could derail an otherwise smooth booking. **Tip 3:** Don't overthink the merger situation. Hawaiian and Alaska remain separate programs today. Book what's in front of you. If you can earn Amex MR points, you can execute this redemption. It's the perfect first award booking for a ChooseFI member who wants to see how the system works without risking complexity.

This sweet spot was last verified over 90 days ago. Award availability and pricing may have changed — verify current rates before booking.

According to recent reports, interisland awards are the key that unlocks multi-island Hawaii vacations without the stacking airfare costs that keep most travelers on a single island. At 7,500-10,000 miles per hop, the points cost is modest, and the trip transformation is significant. Whether you use Hawaiian Airlines miles, Southwest Rapid Rewards, or United partner programs, the strategy is the same: let points handle the short hops so your cash stays in your pocket for experiences. Combined with a points-funded mainland-to-Hawaii flight, interisland awards make a multi-island Hawaiian vacation one of the most achievable aspirational trips in travel rewards.
